---------------------------- MODULE W4Od15m4p6t0 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Traders, Cap

Token(t) == 10 * t

VARIABLES queue, alive, executed, backpressured

vars == <<queue, alive, executed, backpressured>>

Order == [tr : Traders, tok : Nat]

TypeOK ==
    /\ queue \in Seq(Order)
    /\ alive \subseteq Traders
    /\ executed \subseteq Order
    /\ backpressured \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ queue = << >>
    /\ alive = Traders
    /\ executed = {}
    /\ backpressured = FALSE

Submit(t) ==
    /\ t \in alive
    /\ Len(queue) < Cap
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, [tr |-> t, tok |-> Token(t)])
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, executed, backpressured>>

Backpressure(t) ==
    /\ t \in alive
    /\ Len(queue) = Cap
    /\ backpressured' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, alive, executed>>

Crash(t) ==
    /\ t \in alive
    /\ alive' = alive \ {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, executed, backpressured>>

Execute ==
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ LET o == Head(queue) IN
        /\ o.tr \in alive
        /\ o.tok = Token(o.tr)
        /\ executed' = executed \cup {o}
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, backpressured>>

Discard ==
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ LET o == Head(queue) IN
        \/ o.tr \notin alive
        \/ o.tok # Token(o.tr)
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, executed, backpressured>>

Idle ==
    /\ alive = {}
    /\ queue = << >>
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Traders : Submit(t)
    \/ \E t \in Traders : Backpressure(t)
    \/ \E t \in Traders : Crash(t)
    \/ Execute
    \/ Discard
    \/ Idle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AuthorizedMatchingOnly ==
    \A o \in executed : o.tok = Token(o.tr)
=============================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Traders = {1, 2, 3}
    Cap = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT AuthorizedMatchingOnly
nl:
A stock exchange runs an opening auction in which several member traders submit
buy and sell orders into a single admission queue before the market opens. The
queue has a fixed capacity, and when it is full the exchange applies backpressure:
further submissions are refused rather than buffered without bound. Every trader
holds a session token issued at login, and each order it submits is stamped with
that token so the matching engine can tell whose order it is. During the pre-open
window a trader can crash silently, dropping out of the session without notifying
the exchange; such a trader is no longer live and must not be able to place new
orders. The matching engine drains the queue in order: it executes the order at
the head only when the order's stamped token matches the trader's issued session
token, and it discards any head order whose stamp does not match. This guarantees
that no order carrying a forged or wrong session token is ever executed, so no
stale or unauthorized participant can slip an action into the auction.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every executed order carries the exact session token that the exchange issued to the trader who placed it, so no order from a stale or unauthorized session is ever matched.

EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Branches

VARIABLES votes, coordDecision, applied, notified

vars == <<votes, coordDecision, applied, notified>>

Init ==
    /\ votes = [b \in Branches |-> "unknown"]
    /\ coordDecision = "none"
    /\ applied = [b \in Branches |-> "none"]
    /\ notified = {}

Vote(b, v) ==
    /\ votes[b] = "unknown"
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![b] = v]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coordDecision, applied, notified>>

DecideCommit ==
    /\ coordDecision = "none"
    /\ \A b \in Branches : votes[b] = "yes"
    /\ coordDecision' = "commit"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, applied, notified>>

DecideAbort ==
    /\ coordDecision = "none"
    /\ \E b \in Branches : votes[b] = "no"
    /\ coordDecision' = "abort"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, applied, notified>>

Notify(b) ==
    /\ coordDecision # "none"
    /\ b \notin notified
    /\ notified' = notified \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, coordDecision, applied>>

Apply(b) ==
    /\ b \in notified
    /\ applied[b] = "none"
    /\ applied' = [applied EXCEPT ![b] = coordDecision]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, coordDecision, notified>>

Idle ==
    /\ coordDecision # "none"
    /\ \A b \in Branches : applied[b] # "none"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Branches : \E v \in {"yes", "no"} : Vote(b, v)
    \/ DecideCommit
    \/ DecideAbort
    \/ \E b \in Branches : Notify(b)
    \/ \E b \in Branches : Apply(b)
    \/ Idle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CommitOnlyIfUnanimous ==
    \A b \in Branches :
        applied[b] = "commit" => (\A c \in Branches : votes[c] = "yes")

CONSTANTS Branches = {1, 2, 3}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CommitOnlyIfUnanimous
nl:
A regional library network reserves a single rare book across several branch
libraries using a two-phase commit. A coordinator asks each branch to vote on
whether it can honor the reservation. Each branch votes yes or no exactly once.
If every branch votes yes the coordinator decides to commit the loan; if any
branch votes no it decides to abort. The coordinator then broadcasts its decision
to every branch. The network is asynchronous and decision messages can arrive in
any order, and each branch applies the decision it receives to its local ledger.
Applying the decision is the irreversible act of actually lending or releasing the
book, so a branch performs it at most once and only for the coordinator's real
decision. Because the coordinator broadcasts a single decision to all branches,
every branch that acts must reach the same outcome: they can never end up with one
branch having committed the loan while another has aborted it.
SAFETY PROPERTY: a branch applies the commit outcome only when every branch voted yes, so the irreversible loan is committed at most once and never against a no vote.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m4p3t4 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Slots, Jobs

VARIABLES pending, cap, owner, allocLog, backpressured

vars == <<pending, cap, owner, allocLog, backpressured>>

Init ==
    /\ pending = 0
    /\ cap = 2
    /\ owner = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
    /\ allocLog = << >>
    /\ backpressured = FALSE

Enqueue ==
    /\ pending < cap
    /\ pending' = pending + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, owner, allocLog, backpressured>>

Backpressure ==
    /\ pending = cap
    /\ backpressured' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, cap, owner, allocLog>>

Reconfigure(c) ==
    /\ c >= pending
    /\ cap' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, owner, allocLog, backpressured>>

Allocate(s, j) ==
    /\ pending > 0
    /\ owner[s] = 0
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = j]
    /\ allocLog' = Append(allocLog, s)
    /\ pending' = pending - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, backpressured>>

Idle ==
    /\ pending = 0
    /\ \A s \in Slots : owner[s] # 0
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ Enqueue
    \/ Backpressure
    \/ \E c \in {2, 3} : Reconfigure(c)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : \E j \in Jobs : Allocate(s, j)
    \/ Idle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleAllocation ==
    \A i \in DOMAIN allocLog : \A k \in DOMAIN allocLog :
        (i # k /\ allocLog[i] = allocLog[k]) => FALSE

nl:
A network of vending machines is restocked by delivery jobs dispatched from a
central controller. Restock requests arrive into a bounded work queue; when the
queue is at capacity the controller applies backpressure and refuses further
requests rather than growing without bound. The physical dispenser slots across
the machines are a shared resource: each slot can be assigned to at most one
delivery job, because two jobs stocking the same slot would jam or overfill it.
Operators can change the queue capacity at runtime, raising or lowering how many
requests may wait. When a queued request is serviced, the controller assigns it a
free dispenser slot, records the assignment, and consumes one queue slot. Once a
dispenser slot has been assigned it is never handed to a second job. The
assignment log therefore never lists the same dispenser slot twice.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the assignment log never records the same dispenser slot more than once, so no dispenser slot is ever allocated to two different delivery jobs.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od5m5p1t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Players, Quorum, MaxVersion

VARIABLES version, propActive, propBase, votes, commitBases

vars == <<version, propActive, propBase, votes, commitBases>>

Init ==
    /\ version = 0
    /\ propActive = FALSE
    /\ propBase = 0
    /\ votes = {}
    /\ commitBases = << >>

Propose(b) ==
    /\ ~propActive
    /\ version < MaxVersion
    /\ b <= version
    /\ propActive' = TRUE
    /\ propBase' = b
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, commitBases>>

CastVote(p) ==
    /\ propActive
    /\ p \notin votes
    /\ votes' = votes \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, propActive, propBase, commitBases>>

Commit ==
    /\ propActive
    /\ Cardinality(votes) >= Quorum
    /\ propBase = version
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ commitBases' = Append(commitBases, propBase)
    /\ propActive' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<propBase, votes>>

RejectStale ==
    /\ propActive
    /\ propBase # version
    /\ propActive' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, propBase, votes, commitBases>>

Idle ==
    /\ ~propActive
    /\ version = MaxVersion
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in 0..MaxVersion : Propose(b)
    \/ \E p \in Players : CastVote(p)
    \/ Commit
    \/ RejectStale
    \/ Idle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoLostUpdate ==
    \A i \in DOMAIN commitBases : commitBases[i] = i - 1
===========================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Players = {1, 2, 3}
    Quorum = 2
    MaxVersion = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby lets players collaboratively edit a shared match record,
such as the map and rules. Every change must pass a quorum vote: a player proposes
an update, other players vote for it, and it is applied only once at least a quorum
of players have voted in favor. The lobby maintains a version number that advances
by one each time an update is applied. A player may be slow, reading the record at
some earlier point and proposing an update based on the version it saw, but it does
not fail or leave. To avoid lost updates, the lobby applies a proposal only if the
version it was based on still matches the current version; a proposal based on a
stale version is rejected rather than allowed to clobber a newer change. Because
each applied update advances the version by one and is always based on the current
version, the sequence of versions that updates were based on is exactly 0, 1, 2 and
so on, with no gaps and no stale writes slipping through.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the i-th applied update was based on version i-1, so no update ever commits on top of a stale version and no concurrent update is lost.

EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Instances, Capacity, MaxVersion, MaxRetries

VARIABLES inUse, version, claiming, readVersion, retries

vars == <<inUse, version, claiming, readVersion, retries>>

Bump(v) == IF v < MaxVersion THEN v + 1 ELSE v

Init ==
    /\ inUse = 0
    /\ version = 0
    /\ claiming = [i \in Instances |-> FALSE]
    /\ readVersion = [i \in Instances |-> 0]
    /\ retries = 0

BeginClaim(i) ==
    /\ ~claiming[i]
    /\ inUse < Capacity
    /\ claiming' = [claiming EXCEPT ![i] = TRUE]
    /\ readVersion' = [readVersion EXCEPT ![i] = version]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inUse, version, retries>>

CommitClaim(i) ==
    /\ claiming[i]
    /\ readVersion[i] = version
    /\ inUse < Capacity
    /\ inUse' = inUse + 1
    /\ version' = Bump(version)
    /\ claiming' = [claiming EXCEPT ![i] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<readVersion, retries>>

RetryClaim(i) ==
    /\ claiming[i]
    /\ readVersion[i] # version
    /\ claiming' = [claiming EXCEPT ![i] = FALSE]
    /\ retries' = IF retries < MaxRetries THEN retries + 1 ELSE retries
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inUse, version, readVersion>>

Release ==
    /\ inUse > 0
    /\ inUse' = inUse - 1
    /\ version' = Bump(version)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<claiming, readVersion, retries>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances : BeginClaim(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : CommitClaim(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : RetryClaim(i)
    \/ Release

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CapacityNeverExceeded ==
    inUse <= Capacity
===========================================================================

    Instances = {1, 2}
    Capacity = 2
    MaxVersion = 4
    MaxRetries = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CapacityNeverExceeded
nl:
An air-traffic system allocates runways from a single shared pool that is managed
by two independent controller instances for redundancy. Each instance grants
takeoff and landing slots using optimistic locking: it reads a pool version, checks
that a runway appears to be free, and then attempts to commit its grant. The commit
succeeds only if the version it read still matches the current pool version; if
another instance changed the pool in the meantime, the version has moved and the
instance must retry instead of committing on stale information. Committing a grant
increases the number of runways in use and advances the version, while a departing
aircraft releases a runway and also advances the version. No matter how the two
instances interleave their reads, retries, and commits, the number of runways in
use must never exceed the physical capacity of the pool.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of runways in use never exceeds the pool capacity, regardless of how the two controller instances interleave their optimistic grants.

guarded by an optimistic version number. Staff terminals prepare updates by first
reading the current version, then submitting the update to be applied. The network

early version may arrive after the version has already moved on. To prevent lost

against still equals the current version; a submission prepared against a stale

skipped and none consumed twice.

CONSTANTS Rx, Cap

VARIABLES queue, status, dispensedTotal, backpressured

    /\ status = [p \in Rx |-> "new"]
    /\ dispensedTotal = 0
    /\ backpressured = FALSE

    /\ Len(queue) < Cap
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, p)
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![p] = "queued"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<dispensedTotal, backpressured>>

    /\ status[p] = "new"
    /\ Len(queue) = Cap
    /\ backpressured' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, status, dispensedTotal>>

    /\ LET p == Head(queue) IN
        /\ status[p] = "queued"
        /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![p] = "dispensed"]
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ dispensedTotal' = dispensedTotal + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED backpressured

Idle ==
    /\ Len(queue) = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Rx : Enqueue(p)
    \/ \E p \in Rx : Backpressure(p)
    \/ Dispense
    \/ Idle

    Rx = {1, 2, 3}
    Cap = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT DispenseAtMostOnce
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser pulls prescriptions from a bounded fill queue.
When the queue is at capacity, new prescriptions are held back under backpressure
rather than being buffered without limit. A prescription moves from new, to queued
once it enters the fill queue, to dispensed once the pharmacist fills it. Dispensing
is irreversible: handing medication to a patient cannot be undone, so each
prescription must be dispensed at most once. The pharmacist may be slow, taking
arbitrarily long between pulling the next prescription and completing the fill, but
the pharmacist does not fail or abandon the queue. Because a prescription can only be
queued while it is new and can only be dispensed while it is queued, and it never
returns to an earlier state, the total number of dispensing events can never exceed
the number of distinct prescriptions in the system.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the total number of dispensing events never exceeds the number of distinct prescriptions, so no prescription is ever dispensed more than once.

by overwriting another.

vars == <<version, robotState, readVer, target, picked, pickLog>>

Init ==
    /\ version = 0
    /\ robotState = [r \in Robots |-> "idle"]
    /\ readVer = [r \in Robots |-> 0]
    /\ target = [r \in Robots |-> 0]
    /\ picked = {}
    /\ pickLog = << >>

StartRead(r) ==
    /\ robotState[r] = "idle"
    /\ version < MaxVersion
    /\ robotState' = [robotState EXCEPT ![r] = "reading"]
    /\ readVer' = [readVer EXCEPT ![r] = version]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, target, picked, pickLog>>

Claim(r, i) ==
    /\ robotState[r] = "reading"
    /\ readVer[r] = version
    /\ version < MaxVersion
    /\ i \notin picked
    /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![r] = i]
    /\ robotState' = [robotState EXCEPT ![r] = "claimed"]
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<readVer, picked, pickLog>>

Retry(r) ==
    /\ robotState[r] = "reading"
    /\ readVer[r] # version
    /\ robotState' = [robotState EXCEPT ![r] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, readVer, target, picked, pickLog>>

Pick(r) ==
    /\ robotState[r] = "claimed"
    /\ target[r] \notin picked
    /\ picked' = picked \cup {target[r]}
    /\ pickLog' = Append(pickLog, target[r])
    /\ robotState' = [robotState EXCEPT ![r] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, readVer, target>>

    /\ robotState[r] = "reading"
    /\ \A i \in Items : i \in picked
    /\ robotState' = [robotState EXCEPT ![r] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, readVer, target, picked, pickLog>>

    /\ robotState[r] = "claimed"
    /\ target[r] \in picked
    /\ robotState' = [robotState EXCEPT ![r] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, readVer, target, picked, pickLog>>

Idle ==
    /\ version = MaxVersion
    /\ \A r \in Robots : robotState[r] = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Robots : StartRead(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : \E i \in Items : Claim(r, i)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Retry(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Pick(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Abandon(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : AbortRead(r)
    \/ Idle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

    \A i \in DOMAIN pickLog : \A j \in DOMAIN pickLog :

CONSTANTS
    Robots = {1, 2}
    Items = {1, 2}
    MaxVersion = 3
    MaxRetries = 2

NEXT Next
INVARIANT PickedAtMostOnce
nl:
A fleet of warehouse robots picks items off a shared claim board. Each robot works
optimistically: it reads the board's version, targets a free item, and tries to
claim it, but the claim commits only if the board version it read is still current.

retries from a fresh read. Committing a claim advances the board version. A robot can
be slow, lingering arbitrarily long between reading, claiming, and picking, but it

leave the shelf, so it is guarded to fire only for an item not already picked, and
each pick is appended to a pick log. Because picking is gated on the item still being
unpicked, the pick log never contains the same item twice.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the pick log never lists the same item at two different positions, so every item is irreversibly picked at most once.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od11m2p3t2 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Slots, Jobs, Instances

VARIABLES slotState, slotJob, allocLog, instBusy, instSlot

vars == <<slotState, slotJob, allocLog, instBusy, instSlot>>

Init ==
    /\ slotState = [s \in Slots |-> "free"]
    /\ slotJob = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
    /\ allocLog = << >>
    /\ instBusy = [i \in Instances |-> FALSE]
    /\ instSlot = [i \in Instances |-> 0]

Prepare(i, s, j) ==
    /\ ~instBusy[i]
    /\ slotState[s] = "free"
    /\ slotState' = [slotState EXCEPT ![s] = "prepared"]
    /\ slotJob' = [slotJob EXCEPT ![s] = j]
    /\ instBusy' = [instBusy EXCEPT ![i] = TRUE]
    /\ instSlot' = [instSlot EXCEPT ![i] = s]
    /\ UNCHANGED allocLog

CommitInst(i) ==
    /\ instBusy[i]
    /\ slotState[instSlot[i]] = "prepared"
    /\ slotState' = [slotState EXCEPT ![instSlot[i]] = "committed"]
    /\ allocLog' = Append(allocLog, instSlot[i])
    /\ instBusy' = [instBusy EXCEPT ![i] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slotJob, instSlot>>

AbortInst(i) ==
    /\ instBusy[i]
    /\ slotState[instSlot[i]] = "prepared"
    /\ slotState' = [slotState EXCEPT ![instSlot[i]] = "free"]
    /\ slotJob' = [slotJob EXCEPT ![instSlot[i]] = 0]
    /\ instBusy' = [instBusy EXCEPT ![i] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<allocLog, instSlot>>

Idle ==
    /\ \A i \in Instances : ~instBusy[i]
    /\ \A s \in Slots : slotState[s] # "free"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances : \E s \in Slots : \E j \in Jobs : Prepare(i, s, j)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : CommitInst(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : AbortInst(i)
    \/ Idle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleAllocation ==
    \A s \in Slots :
        Cardinality({ k \in DOMAIN allocLog : allocLog[k] = s }) <= 1

nl:
A print shop runs two independent spooler instances that share a single pool of
printer output slots. To place a job in a slot, a spooler runs a two-phase commit
against the slot as participant. In the prepare phase it locks a currently free slot
for a job; the slot then moves to prepared. In the commit phase the spooler finalizes
the allocation and the slot becomes committed, and the allocation is appended to an
allocation log. A prepared allocation may instead be aborted, releasing the slot back
to free. Because a slot can only be locked while it is free, and the two spoolers
contend for the same shared pool through this single lock, no slot is ever finalized
for two different jobs. Consequently the allocation log records each printer slot at
most once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the allocation log records each printer slot at most once, so no output slot is ever double-allocated across the two spooler instances.

----------------------------- MODULE W4Od9m0p6t2 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Instances, MaxEpoch, MaxRetries

VARIABLES epoch, reading, readEpoch, shedLog, retries

vars == <<epoch, reading, readEpoch, shedLog, retries>>

AuthorizedFor(e) == (e % 2) + 1

Bump(n) == IF n < MaxRetries THEN n + 1 ELSE n

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ reading = [i \in Instances |-> FALSE]
    /\ readEpoch = [i \in Instances |-> 0]
    /\ shedLog = << >>
    /\ retries = 0

BeginShed(i) ==
    /\ ~reading[i]
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![i] = TRUE]
    /\ readEpoch' = [readEpoch EXCEPT ![i] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, shedLog, retries>>

CommitShed(i) ==
    /\ reading[i]
    /\ readEpoch[i] = epoch
    /\ i = AuthorizedFor(epoch)
    /\ \A k \in DOMAIN shedLog : shedLog[k].ep # epoch
    /\ shedLog' = Append(shedLog, [inst |-> i, ep |-> epoch])
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![i] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, readEpoch, retries>>

GiveUp(i) ==
    /\ reading[i]
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![i] = FALSE]
    /\ retries' = IF readEpoch[i] # epoch THEN Bump(retries) ELSE retries
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, readEpoch, shedLog>>

Failover ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reading, readEpoch, shedLog, retries>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances : BeginShed(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : CommitShed(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : GiveUp(i)
    \/ Failover

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AuthorizedSheddingOnly ==
    \A k \in DOMAIN shedLog : shedLog[k].inst = AuthorizedFor(shedLog[k].ep)
=============================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Instances = {1, 2}
    MaxEpoch = 3
    MaxRetries = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT AuthorizedSheddingOnly
nl:
A power-grid load shedder is run by two independent controller instances that share
one pool of feeders, for redundancy. Leadership is tracked by an epoch number that
advances on each failover, and for any given epoch exactly one of the two instances
is the authorized leader. A controller sheds load optimistically: it reads the
current epoch, and later commits a shed only if the epoch it read is still current
and it is the authorized leader for that epoch. If a failover advanced the epoch, the
controller's read is stale and it must give up and retry; if it is not the leader for
the current epoch it is unauthorized and likewise cannot commit. Each committed shed
is stamped with the instance that performed it and the epoch it was performed under,
and at most one shed is recorded per epoch. Every recorded shed was therefore
performed by the instance that was the authorized leader for its epoch.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every recorded shed was performed by the instance authorized as leader for that epoch, so no stale or unauthorized controller ever sheds load.

    /\ ver = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
    /\ pend = [r \in Routers |-> 0]
    /\ pendVer = [r \in Routers |-> 0]
    /\ allocLog = << >>

Read(r, s) ==
    /\ pend[r] = 0
    /\ owner[s] = 0
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![r] = s]
    /\ pendVer' = [pendVer EXCEPT ![r] = ver[s]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ver, allocLog>>

Commit(r) ==
    /\ pend[r] # 0
    /\ owner[pend[r]] = 0
    /\ pendVer[r] = ver[pend[r]]
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![pend[r]] = r]
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![pend[r]] = @ + 1]
    /\ allocLog' = Append(allocLog, pend[r])
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![r] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED pendVer

Retry(r) ==
    /\ pend[r] # 0
    /\ (owner[pend[r]] # 0 \/ pendVer[r] # ver[pend[r]])
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![r] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ver, pendVer, allocLog>>

AdminAssign(s) ==
    /\ owner[s] = 0
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = Admin]
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
    /\ allocLog' = Append(allocLog, s)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pend, pendVer>>

    /\ \A s \in Slots : owner[s] # 0
    /\ \A r \in Routers : pend[r] = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

    \/ \E r \in Routers : Commit(r)
    \/ \E r \in Routers : Retry(r)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : AdminAssign(s)

    Routers = {1, 2}
    Slots = {1, 2}
    Admin = 99
INIT Init
NEXT Next

nl:
An airport baggage router assigns bags to a pool of chute slots. Router processes
work optimistically: to take a free slot, a router reads that slot's version, then
commits the assignment only if the slot is still free and its version is unchanged.
If another router grabbed the slot or bumped its version first, the read is stale and
the router retries with a different slot. A committed assignment marks the slot owned,
bumps its version, and appends the slot to an assignment log. A privileged operator
can issue an admin override that directly assigns a still-free slot to a priority bag,
bypassing the optimistic protocol, but it too only takes a slot that is currently
free. Because every path to owning a slot requires that slot to be free at commit
time, no slot is ever assigned twice, and the assignment log lists each slot at most
once.

CONSTANTS Doors, Cap

VARIABLES lockState, lockedCount, unlockedCount, queue, backpressured

vars == <<lockState, lockedCount, unlockedCount, queue, backpressured>>

Total == Cardinality(Doors)

Init ==
    /\ lockState = [d \in Doors |-> "unlocked"]
    /\ lockedCount = 0
    /\ unlockedCount = Total
    /\ queue = << >>
    /\ backpressured = FALSE

EnqueueCmd(d) ==
    /\ Len(queue) < Cap
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, d)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lockState, lockedCount, unlockedCount, backpressured>>

Backpressure(d) ==
    /\ Len(queue) = Cap
    /\ backpressured' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lockState, lockedCount, unlockedCount, queue>>

ProcessLock ==
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ lockState[Head(queue)] = "unlocked"
    /\ lockState' = [lockState EXCEPT ![Head(queue)] = "locked"]
    /\ lockedCount' = lockedCount + 1
    /\ unlockedCount' = unlockedCount - 1
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED backpressured

ProcessUnlock ==
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ lockState[Head(queue)] = "locked"
    /\ lockState' = [lockState EXCEPT ![Head(queue)] = "unlocked"]
    /\ unlockedCount' = unlockedCount + 1
    /\ lockedCount' = lockedCount - 1
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED backpressured

AdminLockAll ==
    /\ lockState' = [d \in Doors |-> "locked"]
    /\ lockedCount' = Total
    /\ unlockedCount' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, backpressured>>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Doors : EnqueueCmd(d)
    \/ \E d \in Doors : Backpressure(d)
    \/ ProcessLock
    \/ ProcessUnlock
    \/ AdminLockAll

    lockedCount + unlockedCount = Total

    Doors = {1, 2}
    Cap = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next

nl:
A smart-home door lock network processes lock and unlock commands through a bounded
work queue. When the queue is full the hub applies backpressure and refuses new
commands instead of buffering without bound. Every door is either locked or unlocked,
and the hub keeps a running count of how many doors are in each state. Processing a
queued command for a door flips that door: an unlocked door becomes locked, moving one
door from the unlocked count to the locked count, and a locked door becomes unlocked,
moving it the other way. A privileged admin override can instantly secure the home by
locking every door and setting the counts accordingly. No command ever creates or
destroys a door; it only moves a door between the locked and unlocked tallies.
Therefore the locked count plus the unlocked count always equals the total number of
doors in the network.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the locked-door count plus the unlocked-door count always equals the total number of doors, so no door is ever created or lost while commands are processed.

----------------------------- MODULE W4Od15m6p6t5 -----------------------------

VARIABLES clock, holder, expiry, orderLog

    /\ holder = 0
    /\ expiry = 0
    /\ orderLog = << >>

    /\ holder = 0
    /\ holder' = m
    /\ expiry' = clock + Duration
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, orderLog>>

    /\ clock < expiry
    /\ Len(orderLog) < MaxOrders
    /\ orderLog' = Append(orderLog, [t |-> clock, exp |-> expiry])
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, holder, expiry>>

    /\ clock < MaxClock
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, expiry, orderLog>>

    /\ holder # 0
    /\ clock >= expiry
    /\ holder' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, expiry, orderLog>>

AdminSeize(m) ==
    /\ holder' = m
    /\ expiry' = clock + Duration
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, orderLog>>

    /\ clock = MaxClock
    /\ holder = 0
    /\ Len(orderLog) = MaxOrders
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

    \/ \E m \in Members : GrantLease(m)
    \/ \E m \in Members : SubmitOrder(m)
    \/ Tick
    \/ ExpireLease
    \/ \E m \in Members : AdminSeize(m)

    Members = {1, 2}
    MaxClock = 3
    Duration = 2
    MaxOrders = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoStaleSubmission
nl:
A stock exchange opening auction grants the right to submit orders through a
time-limited lease. Logical time advances in ticks. When the write lease is free it
can be granted to a member, and the lease is stamped with an expiry a fixed duration
in the future. A member may submit an auction order only while it holds the lease and
the current time is still before the lease's expiry; once time passes the expiry the
lease is stale and must be released rather than used. Each submitted order is recorded
together with the time it was submitted and the expiry of the lease it was submitted
under. A privileged exchange administrator can seize the lease at any time, reassigning
it to a chosen member with a fresh expiry, overriding whoever held it. Because an order
is only ever submitted while the lease is still valid, every recorded order was
submitted strictly before the expiry of the lease it used.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every recorded order was submitted at a time strictly before its lease expiry, so no stale or unauthorized member ever submits an order on an expired lease.

    /\ enrolled = 0
    /\ leader = 0
    /\ alive = Nodes
    /\ term = 0

    /\ leader = 0
    /\ n \in alive
    /\ leader' = n
    /\ term' = Bump(term)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, alive>>

    /\ leader \in alive

    /\ enrolled' = enrolled - 1

    /\ leader' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, term>>

    \/ GrantSeat
    \/ DropSeat
    \/ CrashLeader

nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator leases runways to flights for a limited time. Logical
time advances in ticks. A free runway can be leased to a flight, stamping the lease
with an expiry a fixed duration ahead. Issuing a takeoff clearance for the flight
holding a runway is irreversible, since the aircraft commits to roll, so a flight is
cleared at most once: clearance is guarded to fire only for a flight not already
cleared. A normal clearance is issued only while the lease is still valid, before its
expiry; an expired lease is released instead. A flight may also release its runway
voluntarily. A privileged supervisor can issue an admin override clearance that
bypasses the expiry check, but it too clears a flight only if that flight has not
already been cleared. Because every clearance path refuses to clear an
already-cleared flight, the total number of clearances issued can never exceed the
number of flights.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the total number of takeoff clearances issued never exceeds the number of flights, so the irreversible clearance of any flight happens at most once.
